title: Latin roots I
lede: Well over half of English words trace back to Latin, many of them through French. These twelve roots unlock hundreds of words.

sections.md:
## Twelve high-value Latin roots
| Root | Meaning | Words |
|---|---|---|
| dict | say | predict, contradict, verdict, dictate |
| port | carry | transport, export, portable, report |
| rupt | break | bankrupt, interrupt, disrupt, erupt |
| scrib, script | write | describe, subscription, manuscript |
| spect | look | inspect, prospect, spectator, respect |
| struct | build | construct, structure, instruct, obstruct |
| tract | pull, drag | contract, attract, tractor, extract |
| vid, vis | see | video, evident, vision, revise |
| ject | throw | reject, project, inject, eject |
| mit, miss | send | transmit, permit, mission, dismiss |
| duc, duct | lead | conduct, produce, deduct, educate |
| cred | believe | credit, credible, incredible, credentials |

sections.title: Decoding a business word
steps: It comes from the Italian banca rotta: banca = bench (a money-changer's table), rotta = broken, from the Latin rupt.
The traditional story is that a money-changer who couldn't pay his debts had his bench broken.

sections.title: Stacking a prefix and a root
sections.answer: **To carry across**: moving freight from one place to another.

sections.label: Practice move
sections.md: When you hit a long word, cover the prefix and suffix and look for a root you know. "Unpredictable" = un + pre + dict + able: not able to be said beforehand.

practice.q: A contract "draws" two parties together. Which root shows that?
